items.passage: When Brigid drove the morning route past the cemetery gate in Porto Alegre, Miriam was always waiting there, holding the same cracked umbrella she had mended with wire and tape for three winters. Brigid privately thought the thing was beyond saving; the ribs bent sideways, and rain came through the patches in thin, stubborn threads. Still, each time Miriam climbed aboard and announced that she had fixed it again, Brigid nodded as though hearing news of a small victory. One wet Tuesday Brigid even kept a roll of electrical tape beside the fare box, telling herself it was only for the mirrors. Miriam noticed it, said nothing, and sat in the front seat as usual, shaking water from her sleeves. Outside, the gate's iron rails dripped onto the curb while the engine idled.
items.question: Which choice best describes Brigid's attitude toward Miriam's repairs to the umbrella?
options: She doubts the repairs can succeed but quietly respects and supports the effort.
She is irritated that Miriam wastes her time on a hopeless repair.
She is confident that the umbrella will soon work as well as new.
She feels indifferent and only pretends to listen to stay polite.
items.explanation: Brigid는 우산이 고칠 수 없는 상태라고 속으로 생각하지만(둘째 문장), Miriam이 고쳤다고 말할 때마다 작은 승리처럼 고개를 끄덕인다. 또 요금함 옆에 전기 테이프를 몰래 준비해 두는 행동은 그 노력을 조용히 돕고 싶어 함을 보여 준다. 따라서 회의적이지만 존중하고 지지하는 태도인 A가 정답이다. B는 짜증의 근거가 없고, C는 Brigid의 의심과 반대이며, D는 테이프를 준비한 적극적 행동과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Surabaya's afternoon heat pressed against the windows of the school music room, where Etienne had asked Thuy to meet him beside the old piano. The instrument had belonged jointly to Thuy's late grandfather and Etienne, and a buyer had offered a good price. Thuy came ready to agree; the money would pay for his first year of university. But Etienne only lifted the lid and played a halting tune, missing notes where, he said, the grandfather had always sung over him. Thuy recognized it at once from childhood evenings he had nearly forgotten. Later, walking home, he did not mention the buyer, and Etienne did not ask. Along the canal, vendors were folding their umbrellas, and a boy chased a runaway kite across the bridge.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how Etienne taught Thuy to play a tune on an old piano
To show how a shared memory leads Thuy to reconsider selling the piano
To explain why the buyer's offer for the piano was unusually generous
To suggest that family possessions should never be sold for money
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Thuy는 등록금 때문에 피아노 판매에 동의할 생각으로 왔다. 그러나 Etienne이 할아버지와 함께하던 곡을 연주하자 Thuy는 잊고 있던 어린 시절을 떠올리고, 귀갓길에 구매자 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다. 이 두 지점을 이으면 공유된 기억이 판매 결심을 흔드는 과정을 보여 주는 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 지문에 없는 목적이며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Smoke from the chili oil stung Emiliano's eyes as he ladled broth at the noodle stall in Oaxaca, the stall he had rented from Anacleto for nineteen years. That morning Anacleto had brought papers: the block was being sold, and he was moving to his daughter's city. He offered Emiliano a share of the sale if he would leave quietly by spring. Emiliano listened, then handed him a bowl, as he did every Thursday. When customers came, Anacleto stood behind the counter without being asked and wiped the stools, scolding a boy for dripping sauce, exactly as he had when the stall first opened. By noon the papers lay under a jar of oregano, curling in the steam. Across the street, a bus unloaded schoolchildren in green sweaters.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how Anacleto delivered papers announcing the sale of the block
To explain why the noodle stall had become popular with schoolchildren
To reveal that Anacleto's attachment to the stall complicates his plan to leave
To argue that business arrangements always give way to old friendships
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Anacleto는 건물을 팔고 떠나겠다는 서류를 가져온다. 하지만 이후 그는 부탁받지 않았는데도 카운터 뒤에서 의자를 닦고 손님을 챙기며, 서류는 오레가노 병 아래에 방치된다. 두 장면의 대비는 그가 가게에 대한 애착 때문에 떠나는 계획이 흔들림을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 지문 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: What do you say to a brother who walks back through a door after eleven years? Milena, my sister-in-law, asked me this at the ferry terminal in Gdansk while we waited for Nguyen's boat. I had prepared lists: which rooms of our father's house he could have, which furniture was mine by right. When Nguyen stepped off, carrying one small bag, he did not explain where he had been. He only asked whether the pear tree behind the kitchen still bore fruit. I found myself describing last autumn's harvest in detail, the lists folded and forgotten in my coat. Later Milena laughed that we had divided nothing at all. Gulls circled the terminal roof, and a tugboat sounded twice as it nosed a freighter toward the quay.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount the narrator's trip to meet a ferry arriving in Gdansk
To describe the rooms and furniture of the father's old house
To suggest that family disputes are best settled by forgetting them
To show how the narrator's plan to divide the house gives way to reconnection
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 집의 방과 가구를 나눌 목록을 준비해 둔다. 그러나 Nguyen이 배나무 이야기를 묻자 화자는 수확을 자세히 이야기하며 목록을 잊고, Milena는 아무것도 나누지 않았다고 웃는다. 두 지점의 대비는 분할 계획이 재회의 정으로 바뀌는 과정을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 일화 요약, B는 소재만 쓴 다른 목적, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: "A fine hat, truly fine," Tunde said, turning the wide straw brim in his hands at the dried-riverbed crossing outside Accra. As mayor, he had commissioned it for Ngozi, the town's only doctor, to thank her for a year of night visits. I was twelve and carrying the parcel, so I saw her face before she found her smile: the hat was enormous, trimmed with plastic fruit, nothing she would ever wear. She put it on anyway and walked the whole crossing beside him, nodding at every greeting. Years afterward I learned she had kept it on a peg in her clinic, where patients waiting for stitches would stare at it and forget to be afraid. That afternoon the cracked mud glittered with mica, and goats picked their way along the old banks.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show how Ngozi's polite acceptance of an unsuitable gift turned it into something useful
To describe the appearance of the hat that Tunde had commissioned for the doctor
To explain why the mayor wanted to thank the doctor for a year of night visits
To suggest that people should always be grateful for whatever gifts they receive
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Ngozi는 자신이 절대 쓰지 않을 모자를 받고도 미소를 지으며 쓰고 걸어간다. 뒷부분에서 그녀는 그 모자를 진료소에 걸어 두었고, 환자들이 그것을 보며 두려움을 잊었다고 한다. 두 지점을 이으면 예의 바른 수용이 엉뚱한 선물을 쓸모 있는 것으로 바꾸었다는 A가 정답이다. B는 일화의 묘사만, C는 소재를 쓴 다른 목적, D는 일반적 교훈이다.

items.passage: When Remy arrived at the community garden in Marseille, Noemie was already kneeling among the basil, a notebook open on the soil beside her. For years Remy had owed her uncle money, and her uncle had owed him something too: the fish stew he had cooked at every festival but never written down. Since the funeral, Noemie had asked about the stew twice, each time stopping before she said why. Today Remy did not mention the debt. Instead he pinched a leaf of fennel, named it, and waited while she wrote. Then he named the saffron, the orange peel, the bay. Noemie's pencil moved faster, and she did not look up. Afterward he helped her carry the watering cans to the shed and latched its rusty door.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Remy name the ingredients while Noemie writes?
options: He is embarrassed about the money he owes and wants to change the subject.
He wants to preserve her uncle's unwritten recipe, which Noemie clearly longs for.
He hopes the recipe will earn enough at the festival to repay his debt.
He was asked by the garden's members to record the herbs that grow there.
items.explanation: 지문은 삼촌의 생선 스튜가 한 번도 적힌 적 없다는 점과, Noemie가 장례식 이후 두 번이나 스튜에 대해 물었다는 점을 떨어진 문장에서 보여 준다. 이 두 단서를 이으면 Remy가 재료를 하나씩 불러 주는 것은 그녀가 원하는 레시피를 남겨 주려는 것임을 알 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 다른 감정(당혹)에서 나온 동기, C는 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Years later, Kagiso would still remember the morning the surveyor from the city sat down in his barbershop in Cape Town. Themba had come to measure the farmland Kagiso's family had worked for generations, and the whole street expected a quarrel. Kagiso draped the cape over him and began trimming without a word. Halfway through, Themba remarked that the city's old maps placed the boundary well beyond the stone wall, not along it as the developers claimed. Kagiso paused, scissors raised, and then asked whether those maps could be copied before the hearing. Themba said they could, if someone knew which archive to ask. Kagiso finished the cut slowly and refused payment. Outside, a delivery van idled, its radio playing an old jazz station.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Kagiso most likely refuse Themba's payment?
options: He is still angry with Themba and does not want to accept his money.
He believes refusing payment will guarantee he wins the hearing.
He recognizes that Themba's information about the maps could help protect his land.
He has been told by the street's residents not to charge city officials.
items.explanation: Themba는 옛 지도가 경계를 돌담 너머로 표시한다고 말하고, Kagiso는 그 지도를 청문회 전에 복사할 수 있는지 묻는다. 이 두 문장을 이으면 Kagiso가 Themba를 적이 아닌 협력자로 보게 되었음을 알 수 있어 요금을 받지 않는 이유는 C이다. A는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기, B는 결과를 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Ticking filled every corner of the clock-maker's shop in Seville, dozens of pendulums slightly out of step. Carmela had tended the courtyard garden behind it for thirty years, and Mateo, who had bought the building last month, found her there pruning the orange trees. He told her gently that he planned to pave the courtyard for a café. She thanked him, wiped her shears, and kept cutting, as though the branches still needed her by evening. Inside, Mateo wound a clock that had stopped, and for a moment the shop seemed almost cheerful. Yet each time a bell chimed the hour, Carmela's hands went still among the leaves, and she counted the strokes under her breath. At dusk she swept the fallen blossoms into a neat pile beside the gate.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
options: Cheerful, as the shop comes back to life under its new owner
Hopeful with brief worry, as Carmela trusts the garden will be spared
Peaceful and timeless, as the old shop continues its familiar routines
Wistful, with a quiet sense of loss beneath moments of brightness
items.explanation: 지문에는 Mateo가 시계를 감자 가게가 잠시 밝아지는 순간이 있지만, 정원을 포장한다는 소식 이후 Carmela가 계속 가지치기를 하고 종이 칠 때마다 손을 멈추고 횟수를 세는 장면이 더 두드러진다. 이 두 부분을 종합하면 밝은 순간 아래 상실감이 깔린 아쉬운 분위기인 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, C는 소재와 어울리지만 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Bologna had disappeared under snow by the time Astrid reached the cabin, where Freja was already wrapping their mother's last possession, a chipped blue teapot. They had not spoken in four years. Astrid said she supposed Freja wanted it, since Freja had always been the one who stayed. Freja set the teapot on the table between them and said it was too heavy for one person to carry home anyway. Later, without discussing it, Astrid filled it with water and set it on the stove, and Freja brought down two cups from the shelf, the mismatched ones they had fought over as girls. Neither drank much. Outside, the drifts had buried the fence posts, and a single crow walked across the white yard.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Astrid and Freja?
options: They are wary after a long estrangement but cautiously willing to share again.
Astrid resents Freja, who feels no interest in reconciling with her sister.
Freja depends on Astrid to make every decision about their mother's house.
They are close sisters who have always agreed easily about family matters.
items.explanation: Astrid의 말에는 4년의 단절과 원망이 묻어나지만, Freja는 주전자를 둘 사이 탁자에 놓고 혼자 들고 가기엔 무겁다고 말한다. 이후 Astrid가 차를 끓이고 Freja가 어린 시절 다투던 컵 두 개를 꺼내는 행동은 조심스러운 화해의 몸짓이다. 두 장면을 이으면 경계하면서도 다시 나누려는 관계인 A가 정답이다. B는 한쪽 감정만 반영했고, C는 방향이 반대이며, D는 통념에 기댄 관계로 단절 사실과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Zawadi had not entered the church in Samarkand for six years, so when Linton, the priest, left a basket of cuttings from the parish vines at her door, she assumed it was a reproach. She marched into the vineyard during harvest to return it. Linton, sleeves rolled and hands purple, only asked whether her late husband's rows still grew on the eastern slope. She admitted they did, though badly. He said the cuttings were meant to replace those rows, nothing more, and offered to help her graft them on Saturday. Zawadi hesitated, then took back the basket and told him to bring his own knife, since hers were dull. Pickers called to one another across the terraces, and a cart creaked downhill under its load.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Linton and Zawadi?
options: Linton disapproves of Zawadi and uses the gift to urge her return to church.
Zawadi's initial suspicion gives way to acceptance of Linton's practical kindness.
Zawadi relies on Linton to manage the vineyard rows her husband left behind.
They are rivals who compete each year over whose grapes are harvested first.
items.explanation: Zawadi는 처음 바구니를 꾸짖음으로 오해해 돌려주러 가지만, Linton은 남편의 포도 줄을 대신할 묘목일 뿐이라며 접목을 돕겠다고 한다. Zawadi가 바구니를 다시 받고 칼을 가져오라고 말하는 행동은 의심이 수용으로 바뀌었음을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 Zawadi의 오해만 반영한 관계, C는 의존 방향을 과장했고, D는 통념적 경쟁 관계로 근거가 없다.

items.passage: When the rains flooded the cellar of her house in Haifa, Rivka, a retired judge, summoned her former clerk, Chana, to help carry out the boxes of old case files. Ten years earlier Chana had misfiled an appeal, and a promotion both of them had wanted went to someone else; each still privately blamed the other. Standing knee-deep in the cold water, they lifted the boxes one by one, and the ink on the labels had run so badly that neither could tell whose handwriting was whose. Rivka held a dripping folder up to the light and laughed for the first time that afternoon. By evening the files were spread across the courtyard to dry, every label equally blurred, and Chana, without asking, began sorting them into a single pile rather than two.
items.question: In the text, the blurred labels on the case files most likely represent
options: the damage that the flood caused to Rivka's legal career over the years.
the carelessness that led Chana to misfile an appeal a decade earlier.
the fading of clear lines of blame between Rivka and Chana.
the importance of keeping court records in a dry, safe place.
items.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 승진 실패를 서로의 탓으로 여겨 왔다고 말한 뒤, 물에 번진 라벨 때문에 누구의 글씨인지 알 수 없게 되었다고 묘사한다. 이후 Chana가 서류를 두 더미가 아닌 한 더미로 정리하는 장면이 이어져, 번진 라벨이 책임 소재의 경계가 흐려짐을 상징함을 알 수 있다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 문자 그대로의 홍수 피해에 머물고, B는 과거 실수 자체만 가리켜 상징의 확장된 의미를 놓친다.

items.passage: Joon and Suhyun met on the stone bridge in Busan every evening before their set, as they had for eight years. Lately the duo drew smaller crowds, and both knew why, though neither said it: Suhyun had been offered a solo contract in Seoul. Instead they talked about the bridge. Joon pointed out a crack running between two stones, filled long ago with mortar that had weathered to a different color. Suhyun said the bridge would stand for another century that way. Each night after that, one of them would touch the patched seam while passing, as if checking it. On their last evening before the contract deadline, Suhyun pressed her palm flat against the mortar and held it there, and Joon looked away toward the harbor lights.
items.question: In the text, the mortar-filled crack in the bridge most likely represents
options: the decline in audiences that has troubled the duo's recent performances.
the long history of the city of Busan and its old stone architecture.
Suhyun's confidence that she will succeed in her solo career in Seoul.
the duo's strained partnership, held together by what they avoid saying.
items.explanation: 지문은 두 사람이 Suhyun의 솔로 계약이라는 주제를 말하지 않고 대신 다리 이야기를 한다고 서술한다. 이어서 오래전 메운 균열을 매일 밤 확인하듯 만지고, 마감 전날 Suhyun이 손을 오래 대는 장면이 반복된다. 이 단서들을 이으면 균열과 모르타르는 말하지 않는 것으로 겨우 이어진 듀오의 관계를 상징하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 관객 감소라는 표면 정보, B는 문자 그대로의 의미, C는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: When Neema and Kiara hung their families' tablecloths side by side on the rooftop laundry line in Nairobi, neither said a word, as was their habit after forty years of friendship. Neema's cloth was stiff white cotton for her family's Sunday lunch; Kiara's was patterned in red and gold for the evening feast her relatives were bringing to the same house. The two cloths flapped against each other in the wind, tangling and parting and tangling again, a quarrel conducted entirely in cotton. Kiara reached up once to separate them, then let her hand fall. By late afternoon both were dry, and Neema folded them together, the white inside the red, so they would fit on the one long table downstairs.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a quarrel conducted entirely in cotton” most nearly suggests that
options: the tablecloths' motion expresses the tension the silent friends never voice.
the friends argue loudly about which cloth should be used for the meal.
the cotton cloths are being damaged by the strong wind on the roof.
the two families have refused to share the long table downstairs.
items.explanation: 지문 첫 문장에서 두 친구는 40년 우정 동안 습관처럼 말을 하지 않는다고 하고, 두 집안의 서로 다른 전통이 한 식탁을 나눠야 하는 상황이 제시된다. 바람에 엉키고 떨어지는 천을 말다툼에 비유한 표현은 말로 하지 않는 긴장이 천의 움직임으로 드러난다는 뜻이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 침묵한다는 서술과 모순되고, C는 문자 그대로의 해석이며, D는 마지막에 함께 접어 한 식탁에 올리는 장면과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Who would have guessed that Larissa would end up keeping bees in a Glasgow yard? Twenty years earlier she and her stage partner had toured every hall in Scotland, and Eamon, who had managed them both, now arrived at her gate with news: her old partner was staging a reunion and wanted Larissa to join. Larissa lifted a frame from the hive, heavy with comb, and said she had promised the neighborhood association a season of honey. Eamon watched the bees crawl over her bare wrists without stinging. Her old loyalty tugged at her one way, the new one another, and she stood between them like a hive with two queens, humming and uneasy. She asked him to come back after the harvest, when she might have an answer.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like a hive with two queens” most nearly suggests that Larissa
options: has become an expert beekeeper with an unusually productive hive.
is torn between competing commitments that cannot easily coexist.
feels threatened by her former stage partner's growing fame.
intends to lead both the reunion and the neighborhood association.
items.explanation: 지문은 옛 무대 파트너의 재결합 공연 제안과 동네 협회에 꿀을 약속한 새로운 책임을 함께 제시한다. 바로 앞 문장에서 옛 충성과 새 충성이 서로 다른 방향으로 그녀를 끌어당긴다고 말하므로, 여왕벌이 둘인 벌통은 공존하기 어려운 두 의무 사이의 갈등을 뜻한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 문자 그대로의 해석, C는 근거 없는 감정, D는 두 역할을 다 맡는다는 잘못된 추론이다.

items.passage:
Tell him only that I'm tired, Ruoxi said,
her voice small in the Taipei gym
where her brother's team ran drills beneath the lights.
Nora, who carried words between two languages for pay,
weighed the sentence like a coin with two faces.
The doctor's news sat folded in her pocket,
a paper boat she could not sail across the court.
The boy waved from the free-throw line, grinning,
and Nora waved back, choosing the smaller truth,
while sneakers squealed on the varnished floor
and the scoreboard blinked its patient zeros.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a paper boat she could not sail across the court” most nearly suggests that Nora
options: is unable to read the doctor's handwriting on the folded paper.
wishes she could join the brother's team practice on the court.
cannot bring herself to deliver the serious news to the boy.
plans to give the boy a small gift once the practice ends.
items.explanation: 시에서 Ruoxi는 동생에게 피곤하다고만 전해 달라고 부탁하고, 통역사는 그 문장을 양면 동전처럼 저울질한다. 이후 그녀가 더 작은 진실을 택하며 손을 흔드는 장면과 이어 보면, 코트를 건너 띄울 수 없는 종이배는 의사의 소식을 소년에게 전하지 못하는 마음을 비유한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 종이를 문자 그대로 해석했고, B는 코트라는 단어만 활용한 오독이다.

items.passage: I worked the night shift at a pharmacy in Valparaiso the winter my marriage to Takoda was quietly coming apart, and his mother, Cleotilde, came in nearly every evening near midnight. She bought small things: throat lozenges, a comb, a single bandage. We talked about the fog, the price of oranges, her knees. Neither of us mentioned that Takoda had not slept at home in weeks. Our conversations were a bridge built only to its middle, and each night we walked out to the edge of it, admired the view, and turned back. Once she paused at the door and seemed about to say his name. Instead she pulled her scarf higher and stepped into the wet street, where taxis hissed past under the hill's yellow lamps.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a bridge built only to its middle” most nearly suggests that the conversations
options: were difficult because the two women spoke different languages.
gradually brought the women to an open discussion of the marriage.
took place on the walk from the pharmacy across the town's bridge.
reached toward each other but always stopped short of the real subject.
items.explanation: 화자는 둘이 안개, 오렌지 값, 무릎 이야기만 하고 Takoda가 몇 주째 집에 오지 않은 사실은 꺼내지 않았다고 말한다. 또 Cleotilde가 문 앞에서 그의 이름을 말하려다 멈추는 장면이 이어지므로, 중간까지만 지은 다리는 서로 다가가지만 핵심 주제 앞에서 늘 멈추는 대화를 뜻한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 근거 없는 언어 차이, B는 반대 방향의 진전, C는 문자 그대로의 해석이다.

items.passage: Meera and Eulalio ran rival bakeries on opposite sides of the mountain bus stop outside Lima, and I spent my tenth summer carrying flour sacks for Meera. That year the old master baker of the village died and left his copper dough scraper not to Meera, his apprentice of twenty years, but to Eulalio, who had once insulted his bread in public. For weeks the scraper hung in Eulalio's window, untouched, a medal pinned on the wrong chest. Customers waiting for the bus whispered about it. Eulalio's loaves came out lopsided, and he stopped meeting anyone's eyes. One morning in August I found the scraper wrapped in brown paper on Meera's doorstep, no note attached. The early bus groaned up the switchbacks, its roof stacked with crates of potatoes.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a medal pinned on the wrong chest” most nearly suggests that the scraper
options: was an honor that everyone sensed rightly belonged to someone else.
was a prize Eulalio had won in a public baking competition.
was too valuable to be used for ordinary daily baking.
was displayed to insult Meera in front of the customers.
items.explanation: 지문은 스크레이퍼가 20년 제자인 Meera가 아니라 한때 스승의 빵을 모욕했던 Eulalio에게 남겨졌다고 설명한다. 이후 손님들이 수군대고 Eulalio가 눈을 피하다가 결국 Meera의 문 앞에 두고 가는 장면이 이어져, 잘못된 가슴에 단 훈장은 다른 사람에게 돌아갔어야 할 영예임을 뜻한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 훈장을 문자 그대로 상으로 해석했고, C는 근거가 없으며, D는 Eulalio의 위축된 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: After the worst sardine season anyone in the harbor could remember, Abena, the tenant's daughter, expected Zaynab, the landlord's daughter, to come collecting rent with her usual swagger. Instead Abena watched her walk the length of the quay in silence, stopping at each half-empty boat to ask how the nets had held up. Zaynab wrote nothing in her ledger. When Abena's father apologized for the late payment, Zaynab only shrugged and said the sea had cheated everyone equally. Her manner that morning was so ______ that the fishermen, who had braced for threats, began offering her tea.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: demanding
conciliatory
indifferent
triumphant
items.explanation: 지문은 Zaynab이 평소처럼 거들먹거리며 올 것이라는 예상과 달리 조용히 배마다 그물 상태를 묻고 장부에 아무것도 적지 않았다고 서술한다. 또 늦은 임대료에 대해 바다가 모두를 똑같이 속였다고 말하며, 위협을 대비하던 어부들이 차를 권하게 된다. 이러한 단서는 상대를 달래고 화해하려는 태도를 뜻하는 B 'conciliatory'를 가리킨다. A와 D는 예상된 거만함에 해당하고, C는 Zaynab이 적극적으로 안부를 물은 행동과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Tbilisi's deepest metro platform was nearly empty when Aaliyah, still in muddy boots from three days lost in the hills, sat beside Dainius, the ranger who had found her. A rescue official had just offered him a transfer to an office job in the capital, the way out he had wanted for years. Dainius turned the envelope over without opening it. He talked instead about the trail markers that had washed away and the shelter roof that would not last another winter. When Aaliyah asked whether he would take the offer, his answer was ______: he said it was a good job, that the mountains would manage, and then that perhaps they would not.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: decisive
dismissive
equivocal
enthusiastic
items.explanation: Dainius는 오랫동안 바라던 전근 제안 봉투를 열지 않은 채 산의 표지판과 대피소 지붕 걱정만 이야기한다. 또 빈칸 뒤 대답에서 좋은 자리라고 했다가 산은 괜찮을 것이라고 하고, 다시 아닐지도 모른다고 말을 바꾼다. 두 단서를 이으면 확답을 피하는 애매한 대답을 뜻하는 C 'equivocal'이 정답이다. A와 D는 망설임과 반대이고, B는 제안을 가볍게 무시한다는 뜻이라 그의 고민과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Diesel and river-salt hung over the Galway barge
as Maeve, the ferryman's daughter, cast off the line.
Fergus had paid her twice the fare to reach the far quay
before the bank closed, and they reached it, just in time.
He stepped ashore with the papers signed and sealed,
and she counted the coins, more than a week's wage.
Yet neither smiled. The plan had worked, and still
the success felt ______, a meal that leaves you hungry,
and Fergus lingered at the rail as if he had forgotten something.
She coiled the wet rope, slowly, into the stern.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: deserved
thrilling
permanent
hollow
items.explanation: 시에서 계획은 성공했고 Maeve는 일주일 품삯보다 많은 돈을 받았지만 두 사람 모두 웃지 않는다. 빈칸 바로 뒤의 '먹고도 배고픈 식사'라는 비유와 Fergus가 무언가 잊은 듯 난간에 머무는 모습이 성공이 공허하다는 느낌을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 D 'hollow'가 정답이다. A와 B는 성공의 긍정적 감정이라 웃지 않는 장면과 맞지 않고, C는 문맥과 관련이 없다.
